article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Pineapple-selected Cinderella 99
Breeder: MrSoul / Brothers Grimm Seeds
THC Content: 18–24%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , myrcene , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Overripe pineapple, tropical fruit, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: High to heavy
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Cinderella Pineapple exists because many longtime growers remembered something very specific about early Cinderella 99: the pineapple. Brothers Grimm Seeds developed this version to push that tropical character back to the front, selecting within the C99 family for plants capable of filling a room with the smell of overripe pineapple while retaining the famously fast flowering and energetic personality that made Cinderella 99 so influential. The result was originally known as Pineapple XX and is now sold as Cinderella Pineapple, a name that more clearly connects the cultivar to its genetic foundation.

The appeal goes beyond nostalgia. This is a fast-flowering, sativa-dominant marijuana plant that can produce tight, frosty flowers with foxtailing, vigorous vertical growth, and an unusually loud tropical aroma in roughly two months of bloom. Its experience follows the same direction as its fragrance: bright, euphoric, mentally active, and better suited to creativity or daytime activity than immediate sleep. For anyone who associates classic C99 with pineapple rather than generic sweet fruit, Cinderella Pineapple was bred specifically to recover that expression.
Genetics and Lineage

Cinderella Pineapple comes from within the Cinderella 99 family rather than combining C99 with an unrelated tropical strain. Brothers Grimm used a pineapple-dominant Cinderella 99 selection and crossed it back into Cinderella 99 genetics, concentrating the fruit-forward qualities already present in the line. Earlier releases were marketed as Pineapple XX, while the current name emphasizes what the breeding project was intended to represent: a distinctly pineapple-oriented interpretation of Cinderella 99.

Understanding that distinction requires looking at C99 itself. MrSoul developed Cinderella 99 from Princess and a selected P94 male after several generations of breeding back toward Princess. Princess came from a seed discovered in Jack Herer flower obtained in Amsterdam and stood out for compact growth, very fast flowering, heavy resin, a powerful cerebral experience, and an unusually tropical aroma. Through generations including P50, P75, P88, and P94, MrSoul progressively concentrated those characteristics while reducing unwanted variation.

The pineapple character was already apparent during that process. P75 selections were described as increasingly tropical and pineapple-like, making Cinderella Pineapple less of a new flavor grafted onto C99 than a deliberate return to one of the family’s historic expressions. By selecting and recombining plants that leaned toward that side, Brothers Grimm created a modern feminized line designed to remind growers of the especially fruity Cinderella plants remembered from earlier releases.
Effects and Experience

The experience is typically energetic and mentally uplifting. A moderate amount can bring a quick change in mood, with thoughts feeling lighter and the surrounding environment becoming more interesting. Conversation, music, creative projects, outdoor activity, and social situations often complement this kind of cerebral effect. Rather than producing the slow body heaviness associated with old-school Afghani weed, Cinderella Pineapple tends to encourage engagement.

That stimulation is usually accompanied by euphoria rather than hard-edged intensity when the dose remains reasonable. Focus can become pleasantly flexible, making it easy to move between ideas without necessarily feeling locked into one task. Some consumers describe the experience as motivating, especially earlier in the day, while others find it better suited to unstructured creative time than detailed work requiring rigid concentration.

Higher doses can change the character dramatically. Strong C99-family cannabis has long been associated with a potentially intense cerebral high, and excessive consumption may produce racing thoughts, restlessness, dizziness, or temporary anxiety in sensitive users. Dry mouth and dry eyes are also possible. Smaller servings generally do the best job of preserving the cultivar’s cheerful, tropical, daytime personality without allowing the energetic side to become overwhelming.
Medical Benefits

Cinderella Pineapple may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer an alert experience instead of strong sedation. The uplifting mental character may help some people feel less weighed down by stress, fatigue, or low motivation, while the euphoric phase can make routine activities feel easier to approach. Because THC can affect mood, reward processing, sensory perception, and attention, individual responses can differ substantially even when two people consume flower from the same harvest.

The strain may also make mild physical discomfort feel less intrusive without necessarily producing the heavy body numbness associated with stronger indica cultivars. That balance can be useful for consumers who want to remain active rather than spending the session resting. Appetite may increase, and some people find the gradual relaxation later in the experience useful for reducing general tension, although Cinderella Pineapple is not primarily known as a sedating nighttime weed strain .

Its terpene profile has not been standardized by the breeder, so terpene percentages should be judged from actual laboratory results rather than assumed from the strain name. Limonene is a logical contributor to the citrus and tropical character, while myrcene and beta-caryophyllene commonly provide earthy, herbal, and spicy depth in C99-family flower. None of these compounds should be interpreted as proving a specific medical benefit. Patients should consider cannabinoid testing, personal tolerance, medications, and professional medical guidance when cannabis is being used therapeutically.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Pineapple is the defining feature. Brothers Grimm describes mature plants as capable of producing an especially strong overripe-pineapple aroma, and good examples can smell less like vague tropical fruit than freshly cut pineapple that has begun to become intensely sweet. Citrus peel and lime may sharpen the top of the profile, while sugar-like sweetness gives the fruit a softer background.

Breaking the flowers apart usually makes the tropical character louder. Beneath it, mild earth, herbs, and resin keep the aroma from becoming candy-like. Certain plants may lean toward a fresher pineapple-and-lime direction, while others become richer and almost fermented in their fruitiness. This phenotype variation is expected because the line was created through selection within a broader C99 genetic family rather than engineered around one isolated terpene compound.

The flavor follows the aroma closely. Sweet pineapple can dominate the inhale, followed by citrus and a slightly sharper lime note before a light earthy or herbal finish appears. Vaporization tends to preserve the brightest fruit qualities, while combustion can bring more resin and earth into the finish. Careful drying is particularly important because the volatile compounds responsible for fresh tropical aromas can disappear quickly if flowers are exposed to excessive heat or allowed to dry too aggressively.
Growing Information

Cinderella Pineapple is a fast-flowering sativa-dominant plant with more vertical ambition than its roughly 60-day bloom might suggest. Brothers Grimm recommends allowing seedlings to establish for roughly six to eight weeks before flowering indoors. Young plants can appear lanky, and the cultivar may continue gaining height as bloom begins, making early planning useful in rooms with limited vertical clearance.

The plant responds particularly well to netting. A trellis allows growers to spread the branching structure horizontally while supporting the frosty, tight flowers that develop later. Indoors, topping and low-stress training can also help keep the canopy level, although excessive manipulation is unnecessary if the plant already has sufficient horizontal space. Clones taken from selected plants may remain more compact than the original seedlings, which can make repeat indoor production easier to manage.

Flowering takes around 60 days according to the current breeder guidance, with historical listings often placing the practical window near 56–60 days. That speed is one of the cultivar’s greatest strengths because genuinely sativa-leaning plants often require much longer to mature. Buds can become tight and frosty while retaining some foxtailed structure, giving the flowers a distinctive appearance without developing the loose architecture sometimes associated with tropical-leaning marijuana.

Brothers Grimm characterizes the line as capable of impressive production, particularly when plants receive strong light and adequate nutrition. It is also known for responding well to additional calcium and magnesium when environmental conditions and the growing medium warrant it. That should not be interpreted as a reason to overfeed. Stable root-zone conditions, balanced nutrition, sufficient light, and consistent irrigation remain more important than pushing nutrient concentration beyond what the plant can use.

Outdoors and in greenhouses, size can become considerable. The breeder specifically notes that Cinderella Pineapple may grow extremely tall when allowed to develop unrestricted, making early topping or structural training useful for cultivators who need to control visibility or wind exposure. The relatively short flowering duration can help the strain reach maturity around late September or early October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, though latitude and seasonal conditions ultimately determine the exact harvest window .

Large outdoor plants should be supported before flowers gain their final weight. Netting, stakes, or cages can prevent productive branches from folding during autumn wind or rain. Growers should also preserve airflow through the canopy as flowers tighten. When given strong sun, enough root volume, and favorable weather, Cinderella Pineapple can combine high production with the intense pineapple aroma that defines the entire breeding project.
FAQ
What strains make Cinderella Pineapple?

Brothers Grimm created Cinderella Pineapple from a pineapple-oriented Cinderella 99 selection crossed back into Cinderella 99 genetics. The strain was previously marketed as Pineapple XX. Rather than introducing an unrelated pineapple cultivar, the project concentrates tropical traits already present within the C99 family.
Is Cinderella Pineapple the same as Pineapple XX?

Yes. Pineapple XX was the earlier name used for the Brothers Grimm cultivar now sold as Cinderella Pineapple. The newer name makes its relationship to Cinderella 99 clearer and emphasizes the pineapple expression that the breeder was deliberately trying to recover.
Is Cinderella Pineapple indica or sativa?

It is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Plants can grow tall and energetic, while the effects typically favor euphoria, creativity, sociability, and mental stimulation. Its unusually short flowering period is one reason the Cinderella family became famous: growers can obtain a strongly sativa-style experience without waiting the 11–14 weeks required by many traditional sativas.
What does Cinderella Pineapple taste like?

Overripe pineapple is the main flavor, accompanied by sweet tropical fruit, citrus, lime, mild herbs, and light earth. Some phenotypes are exceptionally pineapple-forward, while others display more general tropical or citrus characteristics. Proper drying and curing are important for preserving the volatile fruit aromas.
How long does Cinderella Pineapple take to flower?

Brothers Grimm currently describes flowering as around 60 days. Historical Pineapple XX material generally places the cultivar near 56–60 days. Outdoors, that relatively fast bloom can produce a late-September to early-October harvest in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, though local photoperiod and weather may shift maturity.
Final Thoughts on Cinderella Pineapple

Cinderella Pineapple is less about inventing a new genetic combination than recovering a particular memory of Cinderella 99. Growers who encountered fruit-heavy C99 plants often remembered intense pineapple as one of the strain’s signature qualities, and Brothers Grimm deliberately selected back toward that expression. The result preserves the core strengths of the family while giving the tropical side center stage.

In the garden, its combination of fast flowering and sativa vigor is especially attractive. Approximately 60 days of bloom is remarkably short for a plant capable of developing tall, energetic growth and an uplifting cerebral experience. Strong production, tight frosty buds, suitability for netting, and vigorous outdoor performance make it more than a novelty flavor selection.

The finished flower is defined by overripe pineapple, citrus, lime, sweetness, and subtle earthy depth. Effects tend to remain bright and active, making the cultivar a better match for creativity and daytime enjoyment than deep evening sedation. High doses can still become mentally intense, especially for consumers sensitive to powerful sativa-style marijuana.

For growers interested in Brothers Grimm history, Cinderella Pineapple also serves as a living link to one of the traits that helped make Cinderella 99 famous. It takes the fast-flowering structure and cerebral personality of the original family and deliberately turns the tropical volume upward. Anyone searching for classic pineapple-forward C99 character will find that this cultivar was created for exactly that purpose.
